what_happened: In job d5gk, the user corrected Athena's second reading of a request about section 10 of ci-routing.md. The reading took in more than one job can finish. The user narrowed it to item 4 only: result reuse keyed by commit, with a local fallback. Items 5 and 6-7 are separate requests. The user's stated reason was that this size fits within one producer deadline. The reading was corrected before the work went on.
cause: Athena builds a reading from the request text and the source document. Nothing makes it compare the reading's size with what one producer run can finish before its fixed deadline. Nothing makes it split a numbered or sectioned document into one job per item. A source such as a design section with items 4 to 7 reads as one outcome, so the reading takes in all of it. Only the user's correction exposed the oversize scope. The reading was not wrong about meaning or audience. It was too big for one job. This differs from the producer-deadline class, where a small job times out. It is the same pressure caught earlier, at the reading.
prevention: Add a sizing step to the reading stage. When a request points at a multi-item source, the reading must list each item. It must then pick one deliverable that fits one producer deadline, and name the other items as separate follow-up requests that are out of scope. The step should reject or split a reading that spans more than one separable item before it is accepted. A code check could count the distinct items or deliverables in a reading and refuse any that exceed the per-job bound.
proposed_request: When Athena reads a request that points at a multi-item source, such as a numbered section of a design document, add a sizing step before the reading is accepted. The reading must list each separable item in the source. It must choose the one item, or the few closely linked items, that one producer run can finish before its deadline. It must name every other item as an out-of-scope follow-up request. A reading that spans more than one separable item, with no stated reason that they must ship together, must be split or refused before the job is admitted. Done when: (1) a test feeds a request naming items 4 to 7 of a sectioned document and the accepted reading covers only item 4 and lists items 5 to 7 as separate follow-ups; (2) a request for a single item passes unchanged; (3) the refusal or split message is worded for whoever runs Athena.
